transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, I suppose I’ve just been feeling a little… constantly on the go, if that makes sense. Even on a quiet day, I’ll be up and moving around, bouncing from the garden club list to my knitting bag to some travel papers, and then I realize I haven’t really finished any one of them. It’s not terrible, I don’t think, but I thought maybe I should ask about it.
When you’re feeling especially on the go, do you find that you need much less sleep than usual?

I don’t think so, no. I mean, I may stay up puttering a little later than I should, but I still feel like I need my usual sleep. I haven’t noticed needing much less or feeling fine on hardly any, if that’s what you mean.
Did you have this same kind of trouble staying focused and finishing things when you were a child?

Yes… I think so, though I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was. I did all right in school, but even in grade school my teachers would tell my mother I was bright, just sort of scattered. I was always misplacing papers, talking when I probably shouldn’t have, and squirming in my seat before I’d finished my work. Does that answer what you mean?
Do these difficulties with staying focused and finishing things cause problems for you in your day-to-day life now?

Yes, I suppose it does, though I hate to make it sound like I’m terribly unreliable. But lately it has put some strain on things at home, and at the community center too. My husband will sort of check behind me, and the other volunteers sometimes have to remind me about plans or details because I don’t always keep them straight. I know they mean well, but it’s embarrassing… and I guess it means they can’t quite count on me the way I’d like them to.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to?

I don’t think I’d say I worry a lot for no reason, no. I mean, I do fret about things sometimes, like anyone would, but usually there’s something I’m thinking about. I haven’t really noticed it being just constant worry out of nowhere… if that makes sense.
